review.assessment: The change introduces `billing/pricing.py`, which computes line totals using standard Python floats and sums them into an invoice total before a single quantization step. It replaces inline billing logic with a structured `Line` class and dedicated pricing functions. This design delegates all monetary rounding to a final `money.quantize` call rather than applying it per-line.

findings.actual: Summing unrounded floating-point values (`running += line.total`) before a single quantization step allows representation errors to accumulate, reproducing the off-by-penny discrepancy described in the task.
findings.at: In `billing/pricing.py`, the `total_of` function accumulates line totals as raw floats and calls `money.quantize` only once at the end. IEEE-754 floating-point arithmetic cannot exactly represent many decimal fractions (e.g., 0.1, 0.2), so repeated addition drifts before the final quantization step catches it.
findings.defect: Floating-point accumulation without intermediate rounding in `total_of`
findings.expected: Invoice total matches the exact sum of per-line amounts, with zero penny-level drift.
